messages:
mira: FYI customer reported a failed SSO login + SCIM provision for the same account. NameID in the SAML looks munged, and our provisioner is throwing a KMS decrypt error. :confused:

sam_dev: can you paste the assertion and the provisioner log?

mira: pasted below (redacted):
```
<saml:Assertion ...>
  <saml:Subject>
    <saml:NameID Format="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress">alice@example.com\u0000\xEF\xBF\xBD</saml:NameID>
  </saml:Subject>
  ...
</saml:Assertion>
```
Provisioner log: `2026-02-12T10:12:03Z ERROR scim-provisioner user=alice@... kms=decrypt failed: tag mismatch or invalid header`

jen_oncall: :eyes: that NUL + replacement-char suggests an encoding/charset got injected upstream. Could be IdP change or our relay (proxy) doing re-encoding. Any recent RBAC/nameid-related deploys?

kevin_sec: We rolled an RBAC rename last week (role:service_writer -> svc_writer) and a short-lived change to the SAML attribute mapping to trim trailing whitespace. Audit shows that mapping change landed 2026-02-11T23:45Z.

sam_dev: OK. Two possible hypotheses: (1) IdP started emitting a non-UTF8 byte sequence in NameID (2) our mapping code does an extra url-encode or truncation that corrupts bytes before KMS envelope lookup. The KMS decrypt error usually means the ciphertext got mangled (different bytes).

mira: I also see a 413/403 pattern in tenant audit: `scim-provisioner -> idp-proxy 400 bad request` then `scim-provisioner -> kms 400 decrypt`. Could be attribute length/encoding mismatch causing the envelope to be re-used incorrectly.

jen_oncall: Repro steps I'd run now: (A) request a fresh SAML login with SAML tracer on browser to capture raw bytes, (B) tail scim-provisioner debug logs with environment var PROVISIONER_DEBUG=1, (C) run a local decrypt of the ciphertext blob we received and compare hex against the one in KMS audit.

sso-monitor-bot: [alert] 2026-02-12T10:05:01Z idp-metadata-change detected (issuer: corp-idp). Metadata diff: removed attribute-mapping:trimNameId=true -> replaced mapping rule.

kevin_sec: That metadata change lines up with the timestamps. I asked IAM team if they pushed a mapping tweak. Waiting on confirmation. Treat as high priority: affects provisioning + KMS integrity.

sam_dev: Quick mitigation: enable a fallback in provisioner to accept unhashed externalId (skip KMS unwrap) for that tenant and alert. Not ideal but will keep users from being deprovisioned. I'll open a canary flag.

mira: Good call. Assigning follow-ups: sam_dev will enable fallback flag + collect raw assertion; jen_oncall will run repro and capture hex blobs; kevin_sec will chase IdP mapping change and ask for rollback if confirmed.

kevin_sec: IAM confirms they deployed a mapping that applies URI-encoding to NameID for legacy SP compatibility. They've rolled it back and will re-run. We should still verify blob integrity.

sam_dev: I enabled the fallback canary for tenant:acme-corp and toggled PROVISIONER_DEBUG. Early results: provisioning resumes for 80% of attempts, but we need to re-onboard those with corrupted blobs. Collected one ciphertext hex: 0x4a6f...9f (attached in channel).

jen_oncall: After rollback, I retried SSO -> assertion bytes no longer have NUL or 0xEF 0xBF 0xBD sequences. KMS decrypt succeeded locally. Looks like IdP mapping was the root cause.

mira: Great. Action items: (1) keep fallback canary enabled for 24h, (2) add an assertion sanity check on our side that rejects url-encoded NameIDs with a clear audit reason (track in ticket), (3) update runbook to include rollback-of-idp-mapping as a mitigation for similar incidents.

kevin_sec: I'll also add an audit hook that alerts when IdP metadata changes include attribute mapping edits.

mira: Thanks team. Filing postmortem once we have numbers on how many accounts were affected. Closing live incident in 1h unless new failures appear. :white_check_mark:
